Implement the final 0423 one-worker design. A session lock is a log record; the existing short file lock remains its own mechanism. Enforce one worker per page, preserve claim ordering, and protect each push with an exact prefix check. 0423 reads the existing book Prime. 0425 will record it. The 0701 trials are separate work orders. After this pass closes and its trial is done, report readiness to Claude for 0426 (t565s2260).

fields.w01: Add `wf lockout <page> <01|04|05> --reason T`. It appends a lockout entry to the log that names the worker (`--as`), the face, the reason, and the start time (the event time). The reason must be non-blank. Refuse any face other than 01, 04 or 05. Refuse if the page already has an unreleased lockout, including a second lock by the same worker or a lock on a different face (no group lockout; one worker per page). The message names the locked face and who holds it. First lockout wins. Put the same rule in Page::order so a log cannot grow a second unreleased lockout. This is not the short .wf-lock file. After a successful lockout, print a Next line that tells the worker to run try-out before work.
fields.w02: Add `wf try-out <page>`. It writes nothing. It reads the log and prints whether an unreleased lockout holds, and if so the face, the worker, the reason and the start time. If none holds, say so plainly. If `--as` is the holder, say the lock holds and that other workers are refused. If `--as` is anyone else, say they would be refused, and name who holds it. Do not treat try-out as applying or releasing a lock.
fields.w03: Add `wf release <page>`. It is accepted only from the worker who applied the unreleased lockout. It appends a release entry that names the face and the lockout entry it closes. After release, the page has no holder. Refuse a release by anyone else, with a message that names who holds it. Also add `wf release <page> --override --reason T` for an abandoned lock. It is accepted from the book's current Prime or from a higher authority (the person / Director). The book's Prime is the current Prime on the book identity page, formed by replacing the work page number with 0000 (for 90.50.10.0423 that is 90.50.10.0000), face 00. Higher authority is the person on that identity page when it exists, otherwise the person on the work page. The reason must be non-blank. Anyone else is refused, including a former book Prime and a work page Prime who is not also the book's Prime. If the identity page or its Prime is missing, do not invent it and do not fall back to the work page's Prime; only the person may override, and the message says the book Prime is missing. Do not init or set-prime the identity page in this pack. The override appends a log entry that names who overrode, whose lock was removed, the face, the lockout entry it closes, and the reason. The log keeps it. Put both release rules in Page::order so a log cannot grow a release by the wrong actor. After a normal release, other workers may lockout. After an override, the same.
fields.w04: Before any work command writes, require an unreleased lockout held by this worker on the face that work belongs to, and treat that check as the try-out on the command itself. Face-write of 01 needs a lockout on 01. Face-write of 04, and draft, need a lockout on 04. Pack, claim, return, check, signoff and close need a lockout on 05. Face-write of 02, 06 or 08 is allowed only to the worker who already holds the unreleased lockout (on 01, 04 or 05), and is refused for everyone else. If no lockout is held, all of these commands refuse, and the message says to lockout first. If another worker holds the lockout, they all refuse, and the message names the locked face and who holds it. --dry-run check also refuses. Keep the existing same-pass claim refusal (first claim wins), and still refuse a second claim on any pass while a claim is open, including by the same worker. Return does not release the face lockout. A check is refused while the builder's lockout is still held, even after return. Two checkers at once are refused, because the first checker's lockout is still held. After release, with no claim open, a new worker may lockout and then claim or check as today (builder may not check its own work). Put the same refusals in Page::order where an event would be appended.
fields.w05: Make push_log, and therefore wf return --push, fetch the published log on the branch (.workshop/logs/<page>/log.jsonl) and refuse unless that log is a prefix of the local log (an exact prefix-extension, including the case where they already match only if there is nothing new to publish). If they diverge, or the published log has a suffix the local log lacks, refuse with a plain message: intake the published log and return again so new events append. Never replace published events. Never force-push. On a lost push race, fetch again and repeat the prefix check; do not pull-merge the log file the way src/cmd.rs:574 does today, because a merge can hide a divergent suffix.
fields.w06: Add tests/page_0423.rs. It must build on Windows: no std::os::unix, and no check command that is only true, grep, or test (stage plan 11.7). Cover: a lockout on 01 that lasts across two face-writes and is still held until release; a refused second lockout on any face while the first is held, including by the same worker; try-out showing the lock holds for the holder and would refuse anyone else; a refused face-write, draft, pack, claim or check with no lockout, and with another worker's lockout; a 05 session of lockout, try-out, claim, return, and a refused check by a second worker until release; a check accepted after release; a refused release by someone other than the holder; an accepted override by the book's Prime (when the identity page records one) or by the person, with a reason, kept in the log; a refused override by a work page Prime who is not the book's Prime; a refused override by a former book Prime; when the book identity page or its Prime is missing, only the person is accepted and the message says the book Prime is missing; a refused push_log when the published log is not a prefix of the local log; and an accepted push when it is a prefix-extension.
